claims.text: Trello Standard costs $6/user/month and Premium costs $12.50/user/month when billed monthly.
Annual billing reduces costs by roughly 20% compared to monthly billing on Standard and Premium.
Trello Enterprise requires a minimum of 50 users and an annual billing commitment.
Nonprofit and educational organizations qualify for a 50% discount on Trello Enterprise.
Organizations on lower-tier Trello plans can add advanced security features for $4 per user per month.
The Free plan limits file attachments to 10MB, while paid plans allow attachments up to 250MB.
Trello does not include native time tracking.
Trello Premium supports six board views: Board, Timeline, Calendar, Dashboard, Map, and Table.
Trello includes automation through Butler and hosts over 200 Power-Up integrations such as calendar views, card repeating, voting, and time tracking.
Trello Free plans allow one Power-Up per board, while paid plans allow unlimited Power-Ups.
Trello Enterprise includes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning via Atlassian Guard Standard, the Observer role, and an Enterprise Admin Dashboard.
Trello Standard and Premium plans lack centralized user deactivation and SCIM provisioning.
All Trello plans include two-factor authentication and unlimited activity logs.
MeisterTask is regarded as the most direct Trello competitor because it also focuses on Kanban, though it offers fewer functions and views.
Asana is priced higher than Trello and targets scaling teams that need flexible project views and robust templates.
ClickUp offers a free plan with unlimited users and tasks, which reviewers consider more generous than Trello’s limited free tier.
Wrike provides more features and views than Trello but is less customizable than ClickUp, and Wrike paid plans are not intended for individual users.
Compared to Jira, Trello lacks built-in development analytics such as velocity tracking and lead/cycle time.
OpenProject, Focalboard, and Taiga are open-source, self-hostable alternatives to Trello.
Trello has more than 50 million users worldwide.
Expert reviewers describe Trello as inexpensive and easy to use but note that teams may outgrow it and that Power-Up add-ons can multiply costs.
TechRepublic assigns Trello an overall rating of 4.26 out of 5.
Trello is commonly recommended for simple projects, small teams, and visual Kanban collaboration.
Trello offers four plans: Free at $0, Standard at $5/user/month, Premium at $10/user/month, and Enterprise from $17.50/user/month when billed annually. (price $0, not found on the cited page)
Academic institutions receive a 75% discount on Trello Standard and Premium plans and a 50% discount on Enterprise. (judge: contradicted)
Trello users can track time through third-party Power-Up integrations including TMetric, TrackingTime, Everhour, and Jibble. (judge: not_stated)
Trello holds a 0.47% market share in the project-management software category as of January 2026. (judge: not_stated)
G2 reviewers rate Trello’s drag-and-drop capability at 94%, its to-do list at 92%, and its task creation and assignment at 92%. (judge: not_stated)
G2 reviewers rate Trello’s AI text generation at 74%, AI text summarization at 75%, and dependencies at 85% among its lowest-scoring features. (judge: not_stated)
